items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: It was like Mr. Cohen. Way back then... I would be second honk with his guys. I'd know if he followed the tune...

ctx.x: We'd have to make sure they were on the front.

We'd have a police stand and everything. Well, the police were standing around the bandstand? I'm saying this because all that's pertaining to jazz, how people respect you if you carry yourself in the right place. Of course, there was some black guys themselves because they were doing things they weren't supposed to. They knew better. I'd do that myself. Somebody don't take advantage of me or take something that belongs to me. You understand? Yeah. I was used to find out. It was like Mr. Cohen. Way back then, if…
Just a few pickpockets, that's all. Nothing serious?
